title: Protocol for structure determination of SARS-CoV-2 main protease at near-physiological-temperature by serial femtosecond crystallography
protocol: Reconstitute pET28a(+) plasmid with EDI ultrapure water.
Spin down the rehydrated plasmid at 5000 rpm for 2 minutes.
Add 25 μL of EDI ultrapure water to the lyophilized plasmid and vortex for 10 seconds.
Repeat the addition and spinning steps three times.
Take Rosetta™ 2 competent cells from -80°C and place them on ice until fully thawed.
Transfer 50 μL of thawed competent cells into a sterile Eppendorf tube.
Add 2 μL of plasmid to the competent cell solution.
Gently mix by pipetting.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 20 minutes.
Apply heat shock at 42°C for exactly 45 seconds.
Place the cells back on ice for 2 minutes.
Add 500 μL of room temperature (22°C) LB medium into the Eppendorf tube containing transformed competent cells.
Incubate the culture tube in an incubator at 37°C for 90 min.
Centrifuge the tube for 2 min at 1500 rpm (238 g) at 22°C.
Discard most of the supernatant by inverting the tube once.
Dissolve the pellet with the leftover supernatant.
Sterilize the spreader with alcohol (70% ethanol).
Burn the tip of the sterilized spreader.
Spread 50 μL of cell suspension onto a kanamycin (50 μg/mL) and chloramphenicol (35 μg/mL)-containing agar plate preheated to 37°C.
Put the plate upside down into a 37°C incubator.
Incubate it for 18 h.
Take out 150 mL LB from 4°C after 18 h of incubation.
Warm the LB medium at 22°C.
Add kanamycin and chloramphenicol antibiotics to 150 mL LB medium in a 1:1000 ratio.
Inoculate the cells into the LB medium by making several streaks in different directions with a pipette tip.
Incubate the starter culture in the incubator shaker at 37°C and 110 rpm for 18 h.
Add 2 mL (1:1000) kanamycin to each of 6 × 2 L LB media prepared beforehand.
Add 2 mL (1:1000) chloramphenicol to each of the 6 × 2 L LB media.
Take out the starter culture from the incubator shaker.
Split the starter culture into two 2 L glass Erlenmeyer flasks containing LB equally.
Incubate the flasks at 37°C and 110 rpm until the growth OD reaches 0.8–1.2 at 600 nm.
Lower the temperature of the incubator shaker to 16°C to cool the cultures.
Add 2 mL (1:1000) of 0.4 M IPTG to each flask once the cultures are cooled down.
Incubate the cultures for 72 hours at 16°C and 110 rpm.
Transfer the cultures into 750 mL Thermo Bottles after induction.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation in an Allegra X-15R Centrifuge at 4°C, 3500 rpm (2850 g) for 45 minutes.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Place four of the centrifuge tubes on crushed ice.
Collect pellets with a sterilized spoon and gently transfer them into 4 × 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Add 25 mL of supernatant to each flask using a serological pipette when the pellet becomes fluid and cannot be collected by spoon.
Transfer dissolved pellets to the same falcon tubes which contain pellets.
Collect remaining dissolved pellets and supernatants until the centrifuge tubes are completely empty.
Spin down 50 mL centrifuge tubes containing bacterial pellets again.
Discard the remaining supernatant.
Store the bacterial pellets in the -80°C freezer.
Take out the samples from -80°C, place them on ice.
Turn on the Beckman Optima™ XL-80K Ultracentrifuge ultracentrifuge beforehand.
Place the Type 45 Ti Fixed-Angle Titanium Rotor inside and set the ultracentrifuge to 4°C from the precool option.
Attach the horn-type Titanium tip to the sonicator.
Clean the sonicator tip with a paper towel sprayed with ethanol.
Add 40 ml Lysis buffer to each sample tube right before sonication.
Set the sonication time to 45 s.
Set the sonication amplitude to 60%.
Sonicate the cell lysate with the cycle above.
Place the next tube in the sonicator.
Apply step 49–51 for each tube.
Repeat step 51 × 4 cycles (or one more cycle after pellet is dissolved).
Clean the sonicator with ethanol and a paper towel.
Transfer the dissolved samples to empty ultracentrifuge tubes.
Balance the centrifuge tubes using the precision scale.
Clean the balance and the bench with paper towels, and turn off the balance.
Close the ultracentrifuge tube lids well, ensure that the plastic caps of the ultracentrifuge tube lids are properly placed.
Dry the centrifuge tubes and inside of the rotor with Kimwipes.
Place the samples inside the rotor according to their balance.
Close the rotor lid well and clean the outside of the rotor.
Check if the O-rings fit well.
Press the VACUUM button on the equipment.
Set up the centrifuge at 40,000 rpm (186,000 g) for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Start the centrifuge.
Release the vacuum after centrifugation is completed.
Take the centrifuge tubes from the rotor.
Transfer supernatants to a sterilized glass bottle placed in an ice box.
Power off the centrifuge after cleaning with a paper towel.
Prepare AKTA GO FPLC system for Nickel affinity purification.
Turn on the AKTA GO FPLC protein purification system.
Clean all the tubes with EDI ultrapure water.
Place the Nickel affinity column to the column port of AKTA GO FPLC.
Wash the column with 3× column volume water.
Wash the column with 2× column volume buffer B.
Equilibrate the column with 3× column volume buffer A (running buffer).
Load the sample to the column at a speed of 2.5 mL per minute.
Take a 40 μL sample from the load and flowthrough.
Mix the sample with 10 μL loading dye for SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Wash the column with 5× column volume of buffer A.
Elute the sample with 2× column volume of buffer B.
Take a 40 μL sample from the elution and mix with 10 μL loading dye.
Check all samples with SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Cut an appropriate length of dialysis membrane and leave it in 22°C water for 10 min to soften.
Close one end of the dialysis membrane with a clip and put the elution sample inside.
Take a 40 μL elution sample and mix with 10 μL loading dye for SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Add 1 μL (2 units) of PreScission Protease for each 100 μg of fusion protein in the eluate.
Add DTT to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM.
Close the other end of the dialysis tube with a clip and check if there is any leakage.
Fill a 2 L beaker with 1.5 L buffer A containing 1 mM DTT.
Put the dialysis tube in the beaker and stir the buffer slowly at 4°C for 5 h on a magnetic stirrer.
Change the dialysis buffer after 5 h to fresh 1.5 L buffer A with 1 mM DTT.
Stir the buffer in the beaker slowly at 4°C for 18 hours.
Transfer the protein solution from the dialysis membrane into a centrifuge tube the next morning.
Spin down the centrifuge tube for 20 min at 3500 rpm (2850 g).
Take a 40 μL sample from the supernatant and pellet.
Mix the sample with 10 μL loading dye for SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Prepare AKTA GO for reverse Nickel affinity purification.
Turn on AKTA GO protein purification system.
Clean all tubes placed in an EDI ultrapure water bottle to flush capillaries and discard remains of previous run.
Place the Nickel affinity column to the column port of AKTA GO.
Wash the column with 3 × column volume water.
Wash the column with 2 × column volume buffer B.
Equilibrate the column with 3 × column volume buffer A.
Load sample to the column at a speed of 0.5 mL per minute.
Collect all flowthrough as a fraction.
Take a 40 μL sample from load and flowthrough.
Mix the sample with 10 μL loading dye for SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Wash the column with 5 × column volume buffer A after loading of the sample is completed.
Elute the uncut protein and Histag from the column with 2 × column volume buffer B.
Take a 40 μL sample from elution.
Mix with 10 μL loading dye.
Check all samples with SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Concentrate protein with a 15 mL 10K cut-off centrifugal concentrator to 10 mg per mL.
Divide the concentrated protein into 1 mL fractions.
Measure the protein concentration by UV absorption spectroscopy using NanoDrop.
Calculate the concentration using the extinction coefficient value and molecular weight from ProtParam tool (ExPASy).
Store the protein aliquots at −80°C after flash freezing with liquid nitrogen.
Crystallize Mpro for structural data collection.
Perform crystallization screening using commercially available crystallization screen kits.
Mix the protein and crystallization screens at a 1:1 ratio for sitting drop, microbatch screening under oil.
Thaw the protein samples stored at -80°C on ice.
Prepare all required materials and tools while the protein samples are thawing.
Set one electronic micropipette to 0.83 μL for protein sample loading.
Set another electronic micropipette to 16.6 μL for paraffin oil loading.
Set a 0.1–2.5 μL micropipette to 0.83 μL for crystallization screen loading.
Label 72-well Terasaki plate with protein name, date, crystallization screen name, and initials.
Fill a 50 mL falcon tube with paraffin oil and place it in a proper rack.
Take the crystallization screen sets (3 boxes, each including 48 different screening conditions).
Open the lid of the Terasaki plate.
Use an electronic micropipette set to 0.83 μL.
Load protein samples of 25 mg/mL concentration into the first two columns (12 wells) in the Terasaki plate.
Load and mix 0.83 μL of each crystallization condition by pipetting gently in a well containing 0.83 μL protein sample.
Cover these 12 wells with paraffin oil using an electronic micropipette set to 16.6 μL.
Repeat the loading, mixing, and covering steps until all wells in the Terasaki plate are loaded.
Cover the plate with the lid.
Keep the plate at 22°C or 4°C room/fridge.
Observe the plate under a light microscope after 1 week of incubation to check for protein crystal formation.
Observe the plate under a light microscope after 2 weeks of incubation to check for protein crystal formation.
Observe the plate under a light microscope after 1 month of incubation to check for protein crystal formation.
Mix 50 μL protein sample with 50 μL crystallization condition in an Eppendorf tube.
Wait 2–3 days for crystal formation.
Vortex the Eppendorf tube containing crystals to create seeds.
Add crystal seeds to the 100 μL protein reservoir mixture solution.
Scale crystals by mixing them to a volume of 100 μL.
Inoculate 1:1 with 1 mL protein reservoir mixture solution using the seeded solution.
Wait 2–3 days for crystal formation.
Mix 10 mL protein sample with 10 mL crystallization condition in a falcon tube.
Use the 1 mL seeded crystal solution to inoculate the 10 mL protein solution.
Grow crystals on a large-scale within 4 days.
Spin down Eppendorf tubes containing screens after several uses (e.g., four times) to prevent evaporation.
Wear laboratory gloves when performing crystallization screens due to potential hazards.
Avoid bubble formation while pipetting during crystallization experiments to prevent unwanted evaporation.
Cover the 50 mL centrifuge tube containing crystals with three layers of organic cotton.
Place the centrifuge tube in a zip lock bag.
Cover the centrifuge bag with cotton.
Transfer the bag into a round plastic container.
Place the plastic container into a styrofoam box.
Fill the empty spaces with cotton.
Ship the styrofoam box in a UN3373 Biological Substance Category B cardboard box.
Load the 1.6 mL sample reservoir with Mpro crystals in unaltered mother liquor.
Inject the samples using Microfluidic Electrokinetic Sample Holder (MESH).
Set the voltage between 2500 and 3000 V, ensuring the counter electrode is grounded.
Adjust the sample flow rate to between 2.5 and 8 μL per minute.
Conduct SFX experiments at ambient temperature at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory.
Focus the LCLS X-ray beam with vertically polarized pulses of 30 fs duration using beryllium compound lenses.
Set the beam size to approximately 6 × 6 μm full width half maximum (FWHM).
Ensure pulse energy is 0.8 mJ and photon energy is 9.8 keV (1.25 Å).
Maintain a repetition rate of 120 Hz during experiments.
Use Psocake software to determine the initial diffraction geometry for ePix10k 2-megapixel detector.
Utilize Cheetah software for data processing.
Monitor crystal hit rates using OM.
Assemble multi-panel detector tiles for detector readout calibration.
Subtract the photon background through radial averaging/median kernel.
Obtain the interactive histogram including Analog to Digital Units (ADUs) in region-of-interest (ROI).
Translate detector into lab coordinates (x, y, z).
Determine hit finding parameters using peakfinder8 algorithm in Cheetah.
Consider a minimum pixel count above 2 and adc-threshold of 500 with a minimum signal to noise ratio of 7 as a peak.
Classify an image with a minimum of 20 peaks as a crystal hit.
Generate small data providing each event including hits, resolution.
Calibrate hits (detector gain threshold applied) and convert to HDF5 file format using Cheetah.
Mask out observable hot pixels and bad detector areas during peak finding by applying a mask in HDF5 format.
Optimize detector geometry by updating the mask.
Optimize mapping of detector panels to the lab frame using geoptimiser.
Complete detector optimization meticulously for accurate peak positions.
Determine unit cell and Bravais lattice type.
Index diffraction patterns with CrystFEL using the correct unit cell and Bravais lattice type.
Display predicted Bragg reflection positions overlaid onto images once indexing is successful.
Ensure observed peaks align with predicted reflections to confirm correct indexing solution.
Adjust integration rings for optimal local background subtraction.
Set narrowest integration radius to size of broadest peak.
Estimate and subtract local background contribution between middle and widest integration radii.
Obtain CrystFEL stream file containing intensity values for every reflection in indexable patterns.
Reiterate through the detector geometry optimization.
Adjust the panel positions relative to the beam for accurate indexing results.
Use CrystFEL version 0.9.0 to index the hits.
Process data from serial crystallography experiments using CrystFEL software.
Integrate and merge the indexed reflections using partialator.
Get .hkl, .hkl1, .hkl2 files from the integration process.
Use check_hkl algorithm to calculate I/σ, completeness from "Merged data (.hkl)" file.
Use compare_hkl algorithm to calculate Rsplit, CC∗ from "Merged half data set A (.hkl1)" and "Merged half data set B (.hkl2)" files.
Determine resolutions cut-offs for the data based on I/σ, completeness, Rsplit, and CC∗ statistics.
Apply the unity model over 3 iterations with max-ADU set to 7500.
Export .mtz file from "Merged data (.hkl)" file via create_mtz algorithm using CCP4's F2MTZ algorithm.
Scale and cut the reflection intensity list by using TRUNCATE software.
Refer to the Wilson plot for determining ideal high resolution cut-off.
Structure determination of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro protein.
Scan the existing structures in the Protein Data Bank using the SWISS-MODEL server.
Select ‘Start Modeling’ on the SWISS-MODEL web server.
Add the FASTA sequence of your protein into the textbox.
Select ‘Search for Templates’ and wait until a list of template results are available.
Select an appropriate model based on coverage of sequence and Identity.
Select the file icon next to ‘Coordinates PDB Format’ to download the structure.
Determine the structure of the crystal form with known space group using PHASER implemented in PHENIX.

Run the command in “Terminal” of macOS or Linux: phenix.automr name.pdb Scaled_name.mtz mass = 30000 resolution=4.0 component_type = protein RMS=0.7 copies=1 space_group=C121 unit_cell = "114 53.5 45 90 102 90" build=False nproc=7 decision_making.use_all_plausible_sg = True
Remove all solvent molecules from the deposited structure for MR.
Open name.pdb and name.mtz files in Terminal using “% cd” command.
Use PDB file obtained through molecular replacement and .mtz file obtained through data collection.
Review residues in the relevant structure one by one in Coot software.
Select File -> Open Coordinates… and choose pdb generated from Molecular Replacement step (MR.1.pdb).
Select File -> Auto Open MTZ… and choose mtz generated from Molecular Replacement step (MR.1.mtz).
Choose ‘Go To Atom…’ or press F6 to center on residue 1 of chain A.
Select ‘Real Space Refine Zone’ or press ‘r’ to locally refine the centered atom.
Press ‘space’ on the keyboard to shift to the next residue in the chain.
Repeat steps 133–136 to iteratively improve your structure.
Check the individual water molecules in Coot program.
Retain positions with strong differential density.
Delete positions without strong differential density by selecting ‘Delete Item…’ in the right action bar, selecting ‘Water’, and clicking on the desired water molecule.
Fill strong empty differential densities with water by selecting ‘Place Atom At Pointer…’ in the right action bar, selecting ‘Water’, and clicking ‘OK’.
Standardize adding water molecules as the last step of structure refinement after protein model has been fully refined.
Upload the final PDBx/mmCIF format to the PDB database.
Convert the coordinate file to mmCIF format using the provided link.
Start the PDB submission from the submission page.
